fields.title: 3. Triggers — Expected vs Actual, Revised Expectation Method
fields.md:
| Trigger | October edition expectation | Actual (10/23) | Verdict | Revised expectation method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T4 Amazon Leo | 2026-4Q ~ 2027-1H | Not started. Next preceding event = Vulcan LV-01 on 10/29 | **Not wrong, but useless** — the start of the window became the launch date, so it fired with no event | Write it not as a window but as **a preceding event + confirmation lag**: one month after the first Vulcan launch (10/29) → recheck on **2026-12-01**, upper bound 2027-1H retained. 'Official pricing page posted' is specified as the confirmation method |
| T5 $40 billion 8-K | 2026-4Q ~ 2027-1H | No 8-K. Press reports price set "next week" | Same problem — fired on the window start date | **2026-10-26 ~ 2026-11-06** (Semafor's "next week" pricing + the 4-business-day 8-K rule, estimated). The measurement layer separately detects 8-K 1.01/2.03 as a 'financing' type event, so the date is an auxiliary line |

(Source: previous value of `state.triggers_next_12m` · Sections 1 and 2 above)

**One-line lesson**: because **window expectations in quarterly or half-year units are read by the measurement layer as the window start date**, an edition opens even when there is no event. Trigger dates should be written as a single checkpoint: "look after this date to find out." This edition paid that cost (one incremental edition with no event).
